narrator.instruct: Gripping, energetic storyteller telling a true, spooky science discovery story with wonder, brisk, excited and punchy, never calm.

anna.instruct: A woman in 1895 staring at an X-ray of her own hand for the first time, gasping in horror and awe.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In a pitch-black lab, the story goes, a professor saw the bones inside his own living hand.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: November eighth, eighteen ninety-five. Wilhelm Röntgen was testing a cathode-ray tube.
lines.say: November eighth, eighteen ninety-five. Wilhelm Rentgen was testing a cathode-ray tube.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He wrapped it in black cardboard, so no light could escape.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But across the room, a screen of barium platinocyanide glowed green.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He blocked it with a thousand-page book, then a board. Still it glowed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then his hand passed in front, and the screen showed his bones.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He spent seven weeks testing the rays.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On December twenty-second, his wife Anna Bertha laid her hand on a photographic plate.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Her bones and wedding ring showed. She reportedly cried out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So how does a ray pass through skin, but not bone?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You see, fast electrons inside the tube slam into the glass and make invisible rays.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Skin lets those rays through. Bone and metal block them and cast a shadow.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He named them X-rays, X for unknown, and sent off his paper on December twenty-eighth.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Within weeks the news circled the world, and doctors were photographing broken bones.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In nineteen oh one, he won the first Nobel Prize in physics. He never patented the rays.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every X-ray you've ever had began with one green glow in the dark.
